versions.label: 1531 Rennes missal (Caen)
versions.date_label: Title imprint 1531, printed at Caen (as described by Duine)
versions.distinctness_basis: The title, as transcribed, says the missal was skilfully emended with several additions and newly joined Masses; Duine lists the Holy Name, Lacryma Christi, Visitation, Roch, Genevieve and Martha. He notes farced Kyries and two Glorias. He also notes that the Mass ends with the Placeat, without a final blessing or last Gospel.
versions.unresolved: No bishop is named. Duine's remark that the Mass ends at the Placeat is his observation of one copy. The 1533 entry may be a second issue of this edition (Duine against Delisle).

versions.label: 1535 Vannes missal (Paris, Yolande Bonhomme)
versions.date_label: Colophon: 10 December 1535 (transcribed by La Borderie, 1891)
versions.distinctness_basis: La Borderie transcribes the title, which calls the book newly emended with many added offices, and the colophon at the foot of fol. 236v. It was printed at Paris by Yolande Bonhomme, widow of Thielman Kerver, for Antoine and Michel les Papolins of Nantes and Guillaume Brunel of the Vannes diocese, on 10 December 1535; he describes a small folio of 240 leaves. Duine reports a copy in the Vannes episcopal library. An old manuscript note in the 1589 breviary, quoted by Duine, says that this missal gave St Denis a sequence and Credo for the whole diocese.
versions.unresolved: Documented from scholarly transcriptions of the title and colophon (La Borderie) and a printing description (Duine); the original was not viewed by this lane. The contents claim about St Denis is second-hand through a manuscript note.

versions.label: 1500 Sées missal (Rouen, for Pierre Regnault)
versions.date_label: Colophon: 1500, day 10 of an unnamed month (read on the original)
versions.distinctness_basis: The colophon says that the missal for the use of the church of Sées, newly corrected and emended ('de novo correctum et emendatum'), was printed at Rouen in the shop of Pierre Regnault, bookseller of the University of Caen, in 1500, on the tenth day of a month left blank. It follows rubrics on defects in the celebration of Mass. The calendar runs from January.
versions.unresolved: The colophon names no bishop. The claim to be newly corrected is the book's own; no predecessor (1488 or 1496) was compared. The copy is incomplete.

versions.label: 1516 Thérouanne missal (Rouen, Martin Morin)
versions.date_label: Final note: 12 November 1516 (as reported in French by the bibliography)
versions.distinctness_basis: The bibliography transcribes the title and reports, without transcribing it, the final note. The missal was printed at the cost of Jean and Antoine Lagache, booksellers at Arras, on 12 November 1516, by Martin Morin at Rouen.
versions.unresolved: Publication facts only; no contents described. Component scope is nominal. Original not viewed.

versions.label: 1631 Noyon missal (Noyon, Michel and Claude Sonnius)
versions.date_label: 1631 as given by Legg; 15 March 1631, Noyon, by Weale–Bohatta (title leaf not inspected)
versions.record_class: provisional-book-state (new stage; downgraded from documented by the independent review)
versions.distinctness_basis: Legg says he examined the Noyon missal of 1631 and did not find directions for mixing the chalice at any time; he contrasts it with the Broglie missal of 1770, which prescribes the preparation during the Kyrie. His remark that the elements would seem to be ready prepared at the offertory anthem is his inference from that absence, not a rubric of the book. Weale–Bohatta give the imprint: Noyon, Michel and Claude Sonnius, 15 March 1631.
versions.unresolved: Cold review 2026-10-22: provisional. The only inspected evidence about the book is Legg's negative observation, which shows nothing positive about its contents and does not prove that the book lacked such a direction; Legg identifies the book by year only, and its title, printer and date come from the Weale–Bohatta entry (bibliographic level). No title leaf, colophon or mandate was inspected. Whether this missal is Roman with a Noyon proper (Ledouble's post-1583 reintroduction) is not stated by either source.

versions.label: Noyon missal of Charles de Broglie (attested by 1774)
versions.date_label: Attested by derivative books of 1774 and 1777; no printing year given
versions.distinctness_basis: The Bibliographie noyonnaise records the title of a Missale Noviomense issued by Bishop Charles de Broglie's authority with chapter consent, known through a 1780 chapter memoir. It lists a 1774 Eucologe and 1777 Heures for Noyon that follow Bourzac's breviary and 'the missal printed by order of Mgr de Broglie'. Legg (1905) cites the book as 'Missale Noviomense (de Broglie episcopo) 1770' and reports its rubrics for preparing the chalice at high Mass, with internal loci.
versions.unresolved: Provisional: no title leaf, colophon or mandate was inspected. Legg's citation gives the imprint year 1770 (matching the catalogue year) and two rubric loci, but not the title or mandate text, so the stage is not upgraded under this lane's rule. The 1774 attestation year is kept as the date of the derivative books.

versions.label: 1776 Rieux missal: the Paris missal issued for Rieux (Bishop de Lastic)
versions.date_label: Title-page imprint 1776 (read on the original); adoption reported in the Nouvelles ecclésiastiques of 6 March 1778 as made 'some time ago'
versions.distinctness_basis: The title page names Bishop Pierre-Joseph de Lastic's authority and the chapter's consent and was printed at Paris for the booksellers of the Paris and Rieux uses in 1776. Its only prefatory letter is Archbishop Vintimille's letter to the Paris clergy dated 11 March 1738, which indicates that the book is the Paris missal issued for Rieux; the Mass texts were not compared. The Nouvelles ecclésiastiques of 6 March 1778 report that Lastic had replaced the Roman books still in use with the Paris breviary and missal, choosing the latest edition with the Sacred Heart office.
versions.unresolved: Upgraded from provisional on the inspected title leaf. The front matter of one copy was read; the Mass texts were not collated against a Paris edition. The Nouvelles ecclésiastiques are a partisan periodical. The periodical names no edition: linking its report to this 1776 book is an inference from the title and front matter, and the Sacred Heart Mass it mentions was not checked in this copy.

versions.label: 1511 Nîmes missal (Lyon, Jean Moylin)
versions.date_label: Colophon: completed 22 October 1511 (read on the original)
versions.distinctness_basis: The title calls the book the missal of the church of Nîmes ('Nemensis'), 'accurate castigatum', under a cardinal's arms with the Briçonnet motto 'Ditat servata fides'. The April calendar keeps the translation of St Baudilius, the Nîmes martyr. The colophon addresses the priests of Nîmes and says that the Lyon bookseller Jean Moylin, alias de Cambray, completed the work at his own expense, at the order and command of the bishop of Nîmes, on 22 October 1511.
versions.unresolved: Five openings were read; no collation. The bishop is not named in the colophon; the Briçonnet identification rests on the motto and the BSG record. The calendar and Masses for the dead are cited as sampled content, not as complete components.

versions.label: 1827 Nîmes diocesan liturgy (Larèche)
versions.date_label: Change dated 1827 by the 1849 survey
versions.distinctness_basis: The 1849 survey says that in 1827 Nîmes left the Roman for an entirely new liturgy composed by the abbé Larèche, vicar general of Bishop de Chaffoy; its table lists Nîmes as having its own liturgy. L'épiscopat français records that the diocesan synod of 27–29 September 1851 decreed the replacement of the Nîmes liturgy by the Roman. Boucarut (1857) says the breviary and missal were given by Bishop de Chaffoy in 1826, adapted from the Besançon books, that the 1835 synod ordered Mass to be said according to the Missale Nemausense, and that the missal differed from the Roman only in its sung parts and some epistles, gospels and orations, keeping the Roman order, Canon and Ordinary.
versions.unresolved: Provisional: no title leaf, colophon or mandate of the Nîmes missal was inspected, so the stage is not upgraded under this lane's rule. The sources date the new books 1826 (Boucarut), 1827 (the 1849 survey and Bergier) and 1831 (the catalogue and Legg's copy); the 1831 witness may be a later printing of the same liturgy.

versions.label: 1766 Mende missal (Paris printing, Bishop de Choiseul-Beaupré)
versions.date_label: 1766 as cited by Legg (title leaf not inspected)
versions.distinctness_basis: Wickham Legg cites the Missale Mimatense, Paris 1766, as his authority for the Mende colour sequence, which he classes as Gallican. The book is the one catalogued from Legg's own collection in the British Library.
versions.unresolved: A one-word classification of the colour rubrics by a scholar who owned the book; no mandate or title text. Whether the 1766 missal follows the 1763 Paris-type breviary (Pascal, Gabalum christianum, 1853, pp. 154 and 266, as read by a lane helper) is not stated by Legg.

versions.label: 1840 Mende missal (Bishop de la Brunière)
versions.date_label: Latin mandement of 25 March 1840 announcing the new missal (Bergier); catalogue printing 1841
versions.distinctness_basis: Bergier reports that Bishop de la Brunière published a new edition of the Mende missal in 1840. The Latin mandement of 25 March 1840 that announced it says that Masses were added, among others, for the octave of Saints Peter and Paul, the Rosary and the Sacred Heart, with a votive Mass of St Privatus.
versions.unresolved: Second-hand report of the mandement; the book was not viewed. The catalogue year 1841 may be the printing of the same edition; identity is assumed at edition level. The additions are relative to the previous Mende missal, which Bergier does not identify.

versions.label: 1485 Tours missal
versions.date_label: Colophon year 1485, as quoted by Van Praet (1824)
versions.distinctness_basis: Van Praet records a folio Tours missal on vellum whose last leaf reads 'Impressum hoc missale Turon. anno domini 1485', with a copy then owned by Chalmel at Tours.
versions.unresolved: Publication facts only; component scope is nominal. Identity with catalogue witness 7610 is assumed at edition level.

versions.label: Tours missal of 1492–1493 (Analecta hymnica siglum C)
versions.date_label: 'imp. Turonis 1492–93' as cited by Analecta hymnica (no leaf inspected)
versions.record_class: provisional-book-state (new stage; downgraded from documented and unlinked by the independent review)
versions.distinctness_basis: Dreves edits the sequence 'Sancti Gatiani laudes' for St Gatian from a fifteenth-century Langres manuscript (Parma) and two printed Tours missals, of 1491 (B) and of Tours 1492–93 (C), recording readings of both.
versions.unresolved: Cold review 2026-10-22: provisional; the exact book is not identified. Weale–Bohatta list no Tours-printed edition of 1492–93: their only 1493 Tours missal (no. 1595) was printed at Rouen by Martin Morin on 17 April 1493, with a copy at Tours, and cites Van Praet no. 366, a Sainte-Geneviève copy whose dominical-letter table begins in 1492. Analecta hymnica's 'imp. Turonis 1492–93' may describe that Rouen edition with a wrong place, or an edition not otherwise recorded. Catalogue witness 7611 (1493, BM Tours) most probably is the Rouen edition, so it is not linked. Attests one local sequence; the original was not viewed. The 1491 print (B) has no separate candidate here.

versions.label: 1529 Saint-Martin of Tours missal (Paris)
versions.date_label: 'imp. Parisiis 1529' as cited by Analecta hymnica (no leaf inspected)
versions.distinctness_basis: Dreves edits the St Catherine sequence 'Ave, virgo generosa' (AH 39 no. 220) from the 1529 Paris-printed missal of St Martin of Tours as his only source, listing three readings he corrected.
versions.unresolved: Attests one sequence. AH 54 (no. 163, p. 253) lists the same book as an uncollated witness of a Trinity sequence. The original was not viewed.

versions.label: 1777 Tulle missal (the Paris missal under a diocesan title)
versions.date_label: 1777 as given by Évenou; the mandate's own date is not quoted
versions.distinctness_basis: Évenou quotes the mandate at the head of the 1777 Missale Tutellense: since the Paris missal had already been received by many churches of France, it should be held beyond reproach, and the bishop offers it to his clergy. He counts Tulle among the dioceses that adopted the Paris missal by giving it a diocesan title.
versions.unresolved: Scholarly quotation of the mandate without its date or locus in the book; the original was not viewed. Which Paris edition was taken over is not stated.

versions.label: 1782 Pamiers missal (Bishop Henri-Gaston de Lévis)
versions.date_label: Title-page imprint 1782; pastoral letter dated Pamiers, 1 June 1781 (read on the original)
versions.distinctness_basis: The title names Bishop Henri-Gaston de Lévis's authority with the chapter's consent; Paris, Claude Simon, 1782. In his letter to the clergy the bishop says that, having issued a new breviary, he had a new missal made to agree with its offices, and that care was taken that nothing in the order or the Canon of the Mass was changed, keeping the norm the Roman Church observes, except that at one or two places, the Commemoration of the living and the prayer after the fraction of the Host, a reading from old sacramentaries and the province's old missals was restored for clarity. He orders all churches, monasteries, colleges and priests of the diocese to use it in solemn and private Masses and no other. The letter is dated at Pamiers on 1 June 1781.
versions.unresolved: Front matter of one copy; the Mass texts were not collated. Bergier (1860, p. 384, read by a lane helper) says Pamiers left the Pius V books in 1781.

versions.label: 1753 Mirepoix missal (Bishop de Champflour)
versions.date_label: 1753 as cited by Chevalier and Weale–Bohatta (title leaf not inspected)
versions.distinctness_basis: Ulysse Chevalier remarks that a prose discussed in a book he reviews is found in the Missale Mirapicense of 1753. Bergier says Mirepoix took the Clermont rite in 1753.
versions.unresolved: Provisional: no title leaf, colophon or mandate of the missal was inspected, the prose is not named on the cited page, and the Clermont attribution is a secondary statement. The companion 1753 breviary's mandate (25 March 1753) dates the reform of the office, not the missal. The Gallica copy (bpt6k325514v) refused access.

versions.label: 1774 Saint-Papoul missal (Bishop Daniel-Bertrand de Langle)
versions.date_label: Title-page imprint 1774; pastoral letter dated 15 August 1773 (read on the original)
versions.distinctness_basis: The title names Bishop Daniel-Bertrand de Langle's authority with the chapter's consent; Toulouse, for the booksellers of the Saint-Papoul uses, 1774. His letter says that the missal completes the recently issued breviary. The introits, graduals, offertories and communions were all taken from Scripture, and the collects, secrets and postcommunions partly from the Roman and partly from the Paris missal, most of them from the Gregorian sacramentary. It is dated at Saint-Papoul on the Assumption, 15 August 1773.
versions.unresolved: The letter's account of sources is the bishop's own; no Mass text was collated. A 1912 bibliography (Bull. Comm. archéol. Narbonne 12, p. 487 no. 2661) dates the book 1773, probably from the letter.

versions.label: Printed Tarentaise missal, undated (assigned to Lyon about 1520–1521 by Analecta hymnica)
versions.date_label: Undated print assigned to Lyon 1520 by Dreves; a Lyon 1521 edition cited elsewhere in Analecta hymnica (no leaf inspected)
versions.record_class: provisional-book-state (new stage; downgraded from documented and unlinked by the independent review)
versions.distinctness_basis: Dreves edits the sequence for St James of Tarentaise, 'Laudum praeconia' (AH 44 no. 167), from a fifteenth-century Tarentaise manuscript missal and the undated printed Tarentaise missal he assigns to Lyon, 1520. AH 40 collates a 'Missale Tharantasiense' printed at Lyon in 1521 for an Epiphany sequence.
versions.unresolved: Cold review 2026-10-22: provisional and not linked to a witness. The print carries no place or date: Dreves supplies '[Lugduni 1520]' in brackets and AH 40 gives 'Lugduni 1521', so the exact book (place, printer, date) is not identified. Weale–Bohatta (no. 1525) list only one printed Tarentaise missal, an undated, incomplete BnF copy, and catalogue witness 7552 ('about 1486', BnF B-1484) is likewise an undated BnF print; both Analecta hymnica editions collate the print against BnF lat. 8889, so it may be that same book. Neither identity nor distinctness is established. The bounds 1520–1521 express the editors' attributed dates, not an inspected imprint; the original was not viewed. The catalogue's '1486 (about)' date is itself unconfirmed (see the gap row).

versions.label: 1491 Saintes missal (Paris, Jean Higman)
versions.date_label: 1491 as cited by Analecta hymnica (title leaf not inspected)
versions.distinctness_basis: Blume and Bannister collate the Paris 1491 Saintes missal as witness B of the Transfiguration sequence 'Haec est dies summe grata' (no. 109), with readings it shares with a fifteenth-century Saintes manuscript missal, and as witness F of a Trinity sequence (no. 162).
versions.unresolved: Attests two sequences in the book. Weale and Misset's Analecta liturgica (pp. 236–247) list some fifty proses from the same print (heading and p. 237 viewed by a lane helper only). An undated Paris-type 'Missale Santonense' (BMC VIII 229–230, IA.41362) is a separate edition not covered here.

versions.label: 1481 Paris Missale Parisiense
versions.date_label: Publication dated 22 September 1481 by colophon
versions.distinctness_basis: The 1481 Paris-use missal has a checked original colophon and bounded Maundy Thursday folios. Neither a first composition date for those prayers nor a predecessor relationship follows.
versions.unresolved: The scan and selected leaves do not certify full physical or textual completeness; 1685, 1705 and 1738 originals are uncollated. GW M24596 cites Ursula Baurmeister's study under 'Zur Datierung'; its full title, '1481: a false landmark in the history of French illustration?', and its place in a bibliographical society's transactions, vol. 11 (1996/99), pp. 350–403, were identified on 2026-10-22 from a bibliography index, but the article itself could not be read (no open copy found). The title suggests that the question concerns the dating of the book's illustration; the colophon year is kept as printed and remains flagged.

versions.label: 1495 Rouen Missale Rothomagense
versions.date_label: Colophon: Rouen, Martin Morin, 18 November 1495 (read on the BSG original)
versions.distinctness_basis: Martin Morin’s identified Rouen print supplies a dated book witness with a contents map; later 1604, 1690 and 1728 entries remain bibliographic successors only.
versions.unresolved: Catalogue page headings are not inspected prayer bodies or proof of a distinct revision or diocesan adoption.

versions.label: 1508 Saint-Ruf missal (Valence, Jean Belon and Pierre de Mole)
versions.date_label: Subscription: last day of April 1508 (transcribed by Chevalier, 1858)
versions.distinctness_basis: Chevalier transcribes the subscription on the recto of the last leaf: the missal for the use of the abbey of Saint-Ruf, ordered and completed, was printed in Valence by Jean Belon and Pierre de Mole, partners, on the last day of April 1508; Belon's mark follows. He describes a quarto in red and black in three parts: 184 numbered leaves, an unnumbered 14-leaf Canon in very large type, and 120 leaves. He says the missal also contains, spread through its parts, the ceremonial proper to the abbey, drawn from the Ordinarium of G. de Nemauso, that of Abbot Lethbert and customs confirmed by general chapters.
versions.unresolved: Scholarly description only; the original was not viewed by this lane. Chevalier calls the book a quarto while the catalogue shelfmark (Mazarine 2°) suggests folio; copy identity with catalogue witness 5825 is assumed at edition level. The ceremonial's sources are Chevalier's attribution.

versions.label: 1529 Saint-Victor missal (Paris, Nicolas Prévost)
versions.date_label: 1529 as cited by Legg; 15 September 1529 by Weale–Bohatta (title leaf not inspected)
versions.distinctness_basis: Legg's table of the times at which the chalice is prepared gives, for the canons of Saint-Victor at Paris, the time 'after vesting and before approaching altar', on the authority of this missal; he could not tell whether the rule concerned solemn or private Mass.
versions.unresolved: One table entry without a folio. The original was not viewed; the day and month come from the bibliography.

versions.label: 1513 Chezal-Benoît missal (Rouen, Martin Morin)
versions.date_label: 1513 as cited by Analecta hymnica (title leaf not inspected)
versions.distinctness_basis: Blume and Bannister edit the Christmas sequence 'Laetare, puerpera' (no. 102) and list the Rouen 1513 Chezal-Benoît missal as witness L. It is not among the witnesses they say they did not collate.
versions.unresolved: Attests one sequence in the book; nothing else about its contents. The original was not viewed.

versions.label: 1527 La Chaise-Dieu missal (Lyon)
versions.date_label: 1527 as cited by Analecta hymnica (title leaf not inspected)
versions.distinctness_basis: Blume and Bannister edit the Marian sequence 'Res est admirabilis' (no. 253) and list the Lyon 1527 La Chaise-Dieu missal as witness U. It is not among the witnesses they say they did not collate.
versions.unresolved: Attests one sequence in the book. The editors cite the same book elsewhere as uncollated. The original was not viewed.

versions.label: 1556 Saint-Remi missal (Reims, Nicolas Bacquenois)
versions.date_label: 1556 as cited by Analecta hymnica (title leaf not inspected)
versions.distinctness_basis: Blume and Bannister edit the Transfiguration sequence 'De parente summo natum' (no. 108) and list the Reims 1556 Saint-Remi missal as witness H, citing its readings in the apparatus. Only the 1506 Noyon missal (F) is named as not collated.
versions.unresolved: Attests one sequence in the book. The title's claim that the book was drawn from manuscripts is not checked. The original was not viewed.

versions.label: Transition french-dioceses-b-batch4:rennes-1492 -> french-dioceses-b-batch4:rennes-1531
versions.record_class: transition removed by the independent review (no named component change); not in the dossier
versions.distinctness_basis: La Borderie says the 1531 Rennes missal reproduces faithfully, with rare variants but with some important additions, the text of the Rennes missal reformed in 1493.
versions.unresolved: Provisional: La Borderie names neither the variants nor the additions, so no component change can be stated. Duine's list of Masses that the 1531 title calls newly added is not a comparison with the 1492/1493 edition. 'Reformed in 1493' is taken to refer to the Guibé edition dated 10 January 1492 (possibly 1493 new style). [Cold review 2026-10-22: removed; La Borderie's statement is kept as evidence on the 1531 stage and in the Rennes gap row.]
